subject: Renewal discussion: add EU + APAC Dedicated pools and throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Sophie Chen <sophie@evergreenai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity at renewal — requirement to expand EU + APAC pools

Hi Rafael,

Quick note as we start our renewal planning: Evergreen's product roadmap has a hard requirement to add two dedicated pools (EU and APAC) when we renew in January. Current usage in NA is steady but we expect a 2.5x peak in Q2 if we enable the new region-specific features.

Can Redwood support the following as part of the renewal amendment?
- Dedicated EU pool: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, 24/7 throughput baseline of 1M tokens/day, regional failover to NA for short outages
- Dedicated APAC pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved, burst capacity of +2x for scheduled launches
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms for EU region, p95 < 180ms for APAC to our SaaS endpoints in Frankfurt and Singapore respectively
- Contract: 12-month renewal with the above pools added to the reserved capacity line item; potential to convert APAC pool to 8x after Q2 if usage justifies it

We also need to understand any additional networking/topology requirements (VPC peering, egress path) and whether SLA credits or penalties differ by region. Procurement will need an amendment draft and any SOC2 / network diagrams to attach to their review.

Appreciate a quick feasibility check — we can schedule a call next week if helpful.

Thanks,
Sophie Chen
Head of Platform
Evergreen AI

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie@evergreenai.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 2 Nov 2025 11:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity at renewal — requirement to expand EU + APAC pools

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask. High level: yes, we can support the EU and APAC dedicated pools at renewal and add region-specific throughput and latency objectives to the amendment.

Notes and clarifications we need before we produce an amendment draft:
- "A100-equivalent": we'll propose exact shapes (8x L40s or 8x A100-equivalent profiles) based on model mix. Can your team share expected percent of long-context generations vs short chat-style traffic? That affects kernel/memory choices.
- Failover behavior: we can configure automatic cross-region fallback but need to align on RPO/RTO expectations and data residency rules. If EU requires data to remain in-region, cross-region failover can only use caching/KV miss strategies rather than full context failover.
- Burst policy for APAC: we can offer burst capacity as a monthly buffer with auto-charge for consumed burst tokens; or pre-provision a higher reserve with discount. Which procurement preference is it?
- Latency SLOs: we can commit to p95 numbers for warmed pools and provide runbooks for on-call and mitigations. SLA credit language will differ for cross-region piping and network-caused anomalies — we'll flag those exceptions in the amendment.

I'll loop Diego (infrastructure/solutions) and Laura (customer success) to surface the technical and onboarding impacts. If this looks good I can produce an amendment outline and a pricing sketch by end of week. Shall I proceed?

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Nov 2025 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Capacity at renewal — requirement to expand EU + APAC pools

Diego / Laura — forwarding Sophie's note. Key asks: 8x reserved EU, 4x reserved APAC (with optional convert to 8x), throughput baselines, p95 latency targets, and network/topology diagrams for procurement.

Diego: can you outline the technical proposal (instance shapes, autoscale triggers, cross-region failover design and limitations, expected token throughput per GPU based on their typical workloads)? Please include networking considerations (VPC peering, NAT egress, private link) and an estimate of time to stand up EU and APAC pools + test plan.

Laura: can you map the onboarding touches and timeline: initial capacity activation, validation, runbook handoff, and escalation path? Procurement will need SOC2 evidence and a short note on data residency.

Respect the constraints Sophie called out about data residency and add any gating items. I'm going to prepare a pricing sketch once we have Diego's shapes and your onboarding timeline.

--

From: Procurement Team <procurement@evergreenai.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 10:24:00 -0800
Subject: Evergreen / Redwood amendment — redlines and payment terms

Rafael,

Thanks for the initial conversations. Procurement reviewed the proposed expansion and attached two requested redlines to the amendment: 1) explicit data residency clause for EU requests; 2) a graduated credits schedule for SLA breaches tied to p95 latency only when the failure is within Redwood-managed infra (network outages excluded).

They also requested:
- Net 45 payment term rather than Net 30 for the new committed capacity line item for the first year (they have internal approvals tied to quarter close)
- A clause allowing Evergreen to convert the APAC pool from 4x to 8x midway through the contract with a 30-day notice and pro-rated pricing adjustment

Please find attached: evergreen_redlines_v1.pdf (redlines inline) and a SOC2 evidence packet request list. We'll need the amended contract and the network diagram for our security reviewers.

Regards,
Evergreen Procurement
procurement@evergreenai.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie@evergreenai.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@evergreenai.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Amendment & onboarding plan — next steps and attachments

Hi Sophie & Procurement team — thanks for the input and redlines. Attached is a draft amendment (redwood_dedicated_amendment_v2.pdf) that:
- Adds EU 8x reserved pool and APAC 4x reserved pool; includes option to convert APAC to 8x with 30-day notice
- Commits to throughput baselines with a monitoring and validation period (30 days post-activation)
- Includes latency SLO language for warmed pools; excludes network-carrier outages from SLA credits as requested
- Adds an explicit EU data residency clause and the proposed Net 45 payment term for the new reserved capacity line item

Diego and Laura have attached a high-level network diagram and onboarding checklist (eu-apac-network-design.png). Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm the redlines look good and return final approval or iterate one more time.
2) Upon approval, sign amendment and we will kick off the EU + APAC pool provisioning (approx. 3 business days for initial config; full validation ~10 business days)
3) Schedule a joint validation call during the 30-day post-activation window to confirm token throughput and p95 latency targets.

I'll place this amendment in HubSpot and send a DocuSign link once Procurement confirms the redlines. 

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_dedicated_amendment_v2.pdf (51 KB), eu-apac-network-design.png (840 KB)
